story: Moritz Simon Geist’s robots make technical techno
text: See also: The Floppotron: Music played on old floppy drives, hard drives, and scanners. [LINK] Animusic: CG animations of fantastic machines playing music. The animation is parameterized to the MIDI input. Attempts to build real-world working models of these machines or machines like them have been made, with varying levels of success: [VIDEO] Compressorhead: An all-robot heavy metal band. Famous for Stickboy, the band's four-armed, headbanging drummer, or at least Stickboy is what I remember most about the band. [LINK]

story: The Alexander: Why did you build such a long piano?
text: Inspired, I presume, by those awesome ray-traced animations from the early oughts? I had started sketching ideas on how to make that a reality (pneumatics and magnets mainly) but never got beyond concept. Specifically this one: [VIDEO]

story: Engineer has built and programmed a terrifying all-robot band
text: Reminds me of a real world Animusic video [VIDEO] Also, at first I thought was going to be the person (or persons) that have their own restored Rock-Afire-Explosion bands and then reprogram them to play contemporary songs.
